item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 7, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, here's what's happening across the media industry.
MIW and the NAB Leadership Foundation are accepting applications for the 2026 LAUNCH Mentorship Program through October 30. Sponsored by Mr. Master, the program now includes women working for broadcast technology partners and vendors, with the selected mentee also attending the 2027 NAB Show in Las Vegas. More information and links to apply are available on Media Jobs Report.
Turning to radio, The Local Media Association has released a new AI roadmap for local broadcasters. Developed with support from the Google News Initiative, the report examines how AI can streamline content production, sales, video distribution and archive searches while keeping journalists and human editorial oversight at the center. More information is available at Media Jobs Report dot com.
In radio news, The National Association of Broadcasters has made two leadership appointments to its Radio Board. Townsquare Media Chief Operating Officer Erik Hellum has been named first vice chair of the Radio Board executive committee. Salem Media Group CEO Dave Santrella has also been appointed to the NAB Radio Board, representing the New England District. Both appointments are effective immediately.
Turning to advertising, CMA has announced five promotions across the organization. Michelle Kirk will lead the CMA Foundation as Executive Director, while Sydnie Hickey moves up to Director of Lifecycle Marketing and Reuben Schwartz becomes Director of Business Intelligence. Ansley Carlson and Katie Karl also received promotions as CMA strengthens several key departments.
Next, Gracie Abrams is heading to New York City for an exclusive SiriusXM Small Stage Series concert at Irving Plaza on October 24. She’ll perform songs from her new album, Daughter from Hell, along with fan favorites. SiriusXM Hits 1 will begin airing the performance October 30, with additional songs featured across several SiriusXM channels.
And finally, 800 Pound Gorilla has named Russell Weissman Head of Licensing. The former All Things Comedy Chief Operating Officer brings more than 15 years of media experience and will help expand licensing, distribution and partnerships as the Nashville-based comedy company continues its growth.
Stay current with more media news, the latest jobs and free industry tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
